articles.title: August's Collabs Corner: Sonic races into Fortnite, Brawl Stars gets an adidas makeover, Nikke meets Persona, and more
articles.summary: Among the updates, announcements and marketing drives for mobile games, this bustling industry sees a never-ending flow of crossovers and collaborations. Some partnerships see characters from one game IP enter another. Others see brands or logos show up in unexpected places.
body: With so many games and so many crossovers, it can be hard to keep track. So, here’s a roundup of the latest collaborations happening on mobile. Stay tuned for more updates.
Learn about collaborations and marketing strategies and make deals at our Pocket Gamer Connects events, such as PGC Nordics in Helsinki on October 20th and 21st.
Fortnite Chapter 7 Season 4: Override is underway, bringing a host of classic game characters and IP into the battle royale.
Sonic the Hedgehog leads the battle pass alongside a Tails sidekick, while the much loved character also gets his own dedicated Green Hill Zone location on Fortnite island.

articles.title: “How did we misjudge this so badly…?” What Supercell learned from upsetting Clash Royale players
articles.summary: Game design lead James Back and community manager Emilia Russell talked through Clash Royale player drama and how to deal with it at Gamescom Dev.
body: Supercell explained some of the thinking behind several major Clash Royale updates that caused community uproar today at Gamescom Dev.
Playing on some of the more extreme feedback the Clash Royale team has received recently, game design lead James Back declared: “At the end of last year, we killed Clash Royale”.
He also admitted that, after several months of fierce, negative player reaction, Back sat at his desk wondering: “How did we misjudge this so badly? Like, how did we get this quite so wrong…?”
Game design lead Back and community manager Emilia Russell then talked through some of the game updates that caused the player discontent, and what they learned from it all.
